- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots after sharp spikes; cap upward revisions after +10% spikes.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days) by forecasting further gains; apply lagged mean reversion correction (e.g., 3-5 day moving average).
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; add a “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment >0.5 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast slope by 10-15%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overpredict late-period prices (last 7-10 days); apply downward bias of 2-5% for final 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversals” (e.g., +0.3 to -0.4), model often misreads momentum; apply smoothing filter: average last 3 sentiment values before forecasting.
